selectedConfiguration: Type89 I-Go Otsu, restored running vehicle at JGSDF Tsuchiura. Primary appearance state is the 2007 Megapixie photograph; 2025 Hunini views corroborate the same preserved car's closed hatches and geometry. Early Ko nose/cupola features are excluded.

dimensionEvidence.adopted: Japanese Type89 summary separates Ko5.75m/Otsu5.70m and gives width2.18m/height2.56m. Independent summaries give5.73m and width2.15-2.18m. The reconstruction records that uncertainty rather than inheriting the legacy game's4.30m normalization.
dimensionEvidence.primarySourceLimit: The referenced original naval equipment table is a lead, not an opened primary measurement: the supplied public JACAR PDF paths returned404. The American1944 handbook calls the later vehicle Model94 and estimates23ft including ditching tail, which conflicts with later summaries; that estimate was not blended into the adopted envelope.
dimensionEvidence.detailDimensions: Wheel stations, panel contours, small fittings and pivots are calibrated from photographs within the nominal envelope. They are reconstruction measurements, not claimed factory dimensions.

sourceAxes: Blender X right, +Y nose, +Z up; metres; ground datum under hull center
runtimeAxes: glTF X right, +Y up, -Z nose; metres; measured vertex cloud and bore direction are validated
inferred: Original1938 paint cannot be established from a restored2007/2025 museum finish. The chosen hue describes photographic restoration appearance, not a factory paint specification.
Hidden engine/turret interiors are dark simplified recesses. Bracket backs, concealed fasteners and small hinge construction not resolved in photographs remain reconstruction.
Contact-band composition is not proven by the available pictures; the dark matte band is a declared material inference.
Micro paint texture, oxide pits and settled dust are physically zoned authoring details calibrated to visible condition, not measured historical damage.
Internal guide depth and wheel running clearance were refined against actual re-imported triangle motion. They are functional visual reconstruction rather than manufacturing dimensions.
The primary 2007 original was recovered during material review (3275x2399). Some other Commons originals remain unavailable and their explicitly labeled standard 1280px thumbnails are retained.

The2007 primary shows an exposed cylindrical perforated bow-MG jacket and an open round cover with an inner five-point badge. The pointed removable cover in2025 photos is a different accessory state and is not substituted into the2007 appearance.
Fine coating grain, shallow cast texture, demonstration speeds and the bow-door gun-stow linkage are explicitly inferred appearance/function choices.
SurfaceV14 fading, primer, edge chips and cavity dust are art-directed age cues, not measurements of the restored car or documented1938 service wear.
V6 battle wear is authored for gameplay; the right side and rear deposits extend adjacent surfaces where no V6 view is available.
historicalBoundary: Museum/same-type appearance references do not establish participation in the16-18March Tengxian city assault. This independent asset does not replace the legacy Type89Tank or change mission history.
accessoryState: 2007 exposed cylindrical perforated bow-MG jacket and opening round cover with inner star; pointed removable2025 cover excluded. Rest joints are closed; the2007 review pose opens them with Type89Motion.
reviewScope: Archived V6 registered front, left and top finish. SurfaceV22 same-camera neutral and raking-light mud review, packed GLB and mechanism tests.

authorization.source: User: first integrate as optional asset after no-major-issue review

surfaceContract.channels: sRGB Base; linear OpenGL Normal; ORM R=AO G=roughness B=metallic
methods: Local cast finish, film roughness, oxide and directional wear evaluated on the calibrated high source
Selected-to-active reprojection into the released G55 UVs with all rigid geometry and transforms held fixed
Retain SurfaceV15 AO, guard alpha and protected badge/non-metal footprints
V6 anchors are traced in the G55 cameras and projected onto visible rest-pose armour.
Bake the finish, shallow relief and local dirt occlusion over the V16 photographed-material calibration; four shoe-local texture variants and independent physical mud deposits.
SurfaceV18 two-distance contact AO from assembled geometry, with separate receiving UVs for rigid moving groups.
SurfaceV19 raises only genuinely exposed steel on the painted impact witnesses, the clean tread lands and the exposed steel jackets.
SurfaceV20 consolidates the opaque body using constant per-primitive UV1 swatches for clearcoat and specular intensity.
SurfaceV21 revises the V6-matched drying mud and sheltered silt, with four shoe coverages and widened original soil geometry.
SurfaceV22 uses CC0 scanned soil relief and drying gradients in four clod tiles and in the existing packed mud on the shoes.

scopeLimitations: Museum appearance and inferred microtexture; no original paint, factory motion-stop or hidden-construction certification.
Photographic perspective and local form matching retain uncertainty; this is not a scan-identical replica.
Door/gun stow linkage is a collision-cleared display reconstruction, not a verified original operating procedure.
